Greetings from MI! I got into fly fishing about 4 years ago and love tying my own flies for me my personal favorites are my deer hair popper, deer hair mouse, and my streamers (big pike and bass fisherman here) I am trying to get into trout and steel head. Could you recommend anything for browns and rainbows?

Every river system is a little different and the fish in those rivers have different flies they enjoy in particular. Seasons make a difference as well. Throwing flies that have been hatching and are active during certain months is usually helpful. Blue winged olives and green drakes are big on Colorado waters. Ive even had success with those patterns in Michigan near Ypsilanti. From what I understand there are decent trout rivers in the UP closer to Canada as trout generally prefer pretty cold water. I would bet mosquito flies would kill it in Michigan for small mouth bass and trout alike. Sometimes you just have to observe the bugs flying around the waters your trying to fish and find something in your arsenal that matches or decently resembles the flies you see.

The appeal...Damn fun to say the least. Fly fishing is one of the oldest forms of recreational fishing as far as western history is concerned. First and foremost I always support state game and fishing regulations. As sportsmen we are responsible for protecting our natural resources and part of that is playing by the rules. Buy your licenses guys, the money goes to under funded departments nationwide.

What fishing is for me is a way to enjoy nature and human ingenuity. As a semi advanced civilization we have more time on our hands than ever before in history. Now I don't know about you folks but I get tired of TV, internet, cultural connectivity to put it simply. Fishing is a release. A challenge. Getting out there and using the tools other clever people have been designing and improving on since one of us thought," hey, fuck it, I just feel like catching a fish for shits and giggles." And that's part of the idea. People do all sorts of things for entertainment. Recreational fishing has just been around longer than xbox.

If your new to fishing or want to give angling a try the best bet is to visit a local shop. Ask some questions, lay it out that you're new and want to get a better idea. Most guys are plenty friendly and are usually more than happy to shoot the shit about fishing till their blue in the face. We are all beginners at one point or another, don't let that stop you.
